raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On gfx1250 the unquantized bf16 lm_head goes through `torch.matmul`, which lands on hipBLASLt and is several times slower than aiter's GEMM at decode batch sizes.

## Modifications

With `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` on gfx1250, a 2D bf16 lm_head matmul uses `aiter.tuned_gemm.tgemm.mm`, as `unquant.py` already does for linear layers on HIP. Other dtypes, shapes and devices keep the existing path. A CPU unit test covers the gate.

## Setup

Kimi-K2-Thinking-MXFP4, TP8, MI455X (gfx1250), image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm10-mi45x-20261019` with sglang 36978d6c4d and aiter 2bb549102 plus Kimi-K2 GEMM configs.

Server: `--tp 8 --attention-backend aiter --prefill-attention-backend aiter --decode-attention-backend aiter --page-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --disable-radix-cache --disable-custom-all-reduce --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 128 --max-running-requests 128 --mem-fraction-static 0.8`.

## Accuracy Tests

The lm_head output is bit-identical to `torch.mm` at batch sizes 1, 4, 32 and 128.

GSM8K with `few_shot_gsm8k` (8-shot, 1319 questions, `max_new_tokens` 512, the settings of sglang's AMD Kimi accuracy tests):

| | Accuracy | Invalid |
|---|---|---|
| Before (two runs) | 0.939 / 0.945 | 0.000 / 0.000 |
| After | 0.944 | 0.000 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

lm_head of Kimi-K2 at TP8 (vocab shard 20480 x 7168, 293 MB of weights, far larger than L2), MI455X, CUDA-graph replay:

| batch | torch.mm (ms) | tgemm.mm (ms) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.131 | 0.070 |
| 4 | 0.129 | 0.062 |
| 32 | 0.285 | 0.074 |
| 128 | 0.986 | 0.232 |

End to end, TP8, 8k input / 1k output, concurrency 4, `bench_serving`:

| | Output tok/s | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before | 137.42 | 414.54 | 27.90 |
| After | 142.08 (+3.4%) | 414.09 | 26.92 (-3.5%) |

At batch 4 the kernel saves about 0.07 ms per decode step, so most of the end-to-end difference is run-to-run variance (the two before runs differ by 2.1%); the saving grows with batch size (0.75 ms per step at batch 128).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

## CI Status for PR #44455

**Verdict:** None of the 3 executed failures was caused by this PR. Its only runtime change is gated to gfx1250, and the failing jobs ran on gfx950 and on Xeon CPU. PR CI is **not complete**: 2 AMD mi35x shards in `pr-test-amd.yml` and 1 job in `pr-test.yml` are still queued.

> [!NOTE]

|-----|------|---------|-----------|----------|-----|
| [`stage-b-test-large-8-gpu-mi35x-disaggregation-amd (rocm10)`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39449962492/job/122579187704) | `test/registered/amd/disaggregation/test_disaggregation_basic.py::TestDisaggregationAccuracy.setUpClass` | `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: out of memory` (hipErrorOutOfMemory) at `scheduler.py:1951` `run_event_loop`. Both the prefill and decode servers crashed in the same second (02:31:48), right after Mooncake `RdmaTransport: registered 82 buffers`. Server startup crash, 1 attempt (`logs/122579187704.log` lines 5927–5952) | Comparable rocm10 runs (same GPU, same image line, same launch config) passed: 0.950/0.950 ([F1.M5](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40250572724/job/121341392609)), 0.950/0.950 ([F1.M4](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40333555627/job/121609122887)), 0.955/0.950 ([F1.M1](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40427865857/job/121938136610)). None of the 3 has the OOM. The newer `main` legs rocm724 ([job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40552180703/job/122358686020)) and rocm720 ([job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40552180703/job/122358686120)) fail this test differently (accuracy 0.0–0.005), so they are not comparable | 🟢 | **Independence.** The new path is gated by `_use_aiter_lm_head = is_hip() and SGLANG_USE_AITER and is_gfx1250_supported()` (D2). `is_gfx1250_supported()` checks `gcnArchName` for `gfx1250` (`python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py:1262`), and this job ran on gfx950 (`F1.env`). So `tgemm` is never imported, and `_aiter_lm_head_ok` short-circuits to False (D3). No GEMM/tgemm AITER module loaded (`F1.markers`). The module-level `get_device_properties(0)` call adds nothing: `memory_pool.py:121` and `fp8.py:133` already make the same call at import on ROCm. The prefill server, which ran no lm_head forward (`cuda_graph` all 0.00), OOM'd at the same moment as the decode server. **Against:** this is a new failure mode compared with comparable `main` runs, and the merge base [`eb4b167d`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/eb4b167d2749840eae18167fe9e0a608308e45aa) carries `main` commits newer than F1.M1, so a recent `main` change or a transient runner/RDMA problem is still possible |

Both tests should pass once the image is built from a base that contains [#43341](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43341) and [#40900](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40900). detail.title: [Perf] [AMD] lm_head: Use aiter tgemm for the bf16 lm_head on gfx1250

files.patch:
@@ -69,6 +69,8 @@
 )
 from sglang.srt.utils.common import (
     is_cpu,
+    is_gfx1250_supported,
+    is_hip,
     is_npu,
     is_pin_memory_available,
     use_intel_amx_backend,
@@ -78,6 +80,19 @@
 
 _is_npu = is_npu()
 _is_cpu = is_cpu()
+# On gfx1250, torch.mm for a bf16 lm_head is slower than aiter's GEMM.
+_use_aiter_lm_head = is_hip() and envs.SGLANG_USE_AITER.get() and is_gfx1250_supported()
+if _use_aiter_lm_head:
+    from aiter.tuned_gemm import tgemm
+
+
+def _aiter_lm_head_ok(hidden_states: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor) -> bool:
+    return (
+        _use_aiter_lm_head
+        and hidden_states.dim() == 2
+        and hidden_states.dtype == weight.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+    )
+
 
 _UNQUANTIZED_LM_HEAD_METHODS = {
     "UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod",
@@ -1102,6 +1117,8 @@ def _compute_lm_head(
                 logits = torch.matmul(
                     hidden_states.bfloat16(), lm_head.weight.T.bfloat16()
                 )
+            elif _aiter_lm_head_ok(hidden_states, lm_head.weight):
+                logits = tgemm.mm(hidden_states, lm_head.weight)
             else:
                 logits = torch.matmul(
                     hidden_states.to(lm_head.weight.dtype), lm_head.weight.T

@@ -0,0 +1,53 @@
+"""When the lm_head matmul goes through aiter tgemm on gfx1250.
+
+tgemm.mm takes a 2D bf16 activation and a bf16 weight; any other shape or
+dtype keeps torch.matmul.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+from unittest import mock
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers import logits_processor
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+_VOCAB = 32
+_HIDDEN = 16
+
+
+def _ok(hidden_shape=(4, _HIDDEN), hidden_dtype=torch.bfloat16, weight_dtype=None):
+    hidden_states = torch.zeros(hidden_shape, dtype=hidden_dtype)
+    weight = torch.zeros((_VOCAB, _HIDDEN), dtype=weight_dtype or hidden_dtype)
+    return logits_processor._aiter_lm_head_ok(hidden_states, weight)
+
+
+class TestAiterLmHeadGate(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        patcher = mock.patch.object(logits_processor, "_use_aiter_lm_head", True)
+        patcher.start()
+        self.addCleanup(patcher.stop)
+
+    def test_2d_bf16_uses_tgemm(self):
+        self.assertTrue(_ok())
+
+    def test_off_gfx1250_keeps_torch_matmul(self):
+        with mock.patch.object(logits_processor, "_use_aiter_lm_head", False):
+            self.assertFalse(_ok())
+
+    def test_other_shapes_and_dtypes_keep_torch_matmul(self):
+        for kwargs in (
+            dict(hidden_shape=(2, 4, _HIDDEN)),
+            dict(hidden_dtype=torch.float16),
+            dict(hidden_dtype=torch.float32),
+            dict(weight_dtype=torch.float32),
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(**{k: str(v) for k, v in kwargs.items()}):
+                self.assertFalse(_ok(**kwargs))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
